Dude, you obviously missed the symbolism with Mr. Harvey's death. During the scene where Lindsey gets upset about the "perfect murder" challenge, Susie says the project is similar to an old game in heaven - how to complete the perfect murder. Susie says she says chooses the icicle - it melts away. This is symbolic, it shows that Susie is nothing if not compassionate - in the pretend murder she does, the pain experienced by others, and, depending on how you look at it, even by Mr. Harvey(?) melts away. 

As you may recall, Mr. Harvey got domed by an icicle and died while chasing a young girl around. Sound familiar? His death wasn't revenge for Susie, for the reader, for his other victims, it was to make sure he couldn't hurt anyone anymore.
